<solution_file path="src/solution.py">
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

def main():
    # Read the raw Eurostat data
    df = pd.read_csv('outputs/t02_eurostat_raw.csv')

    # Identify all unique indicator_ids in their order of first appearance
    # This ensures we have a complete list of columns to include in the final matrix
    indicator_ids = df['indicator_id'].unique().tolist()

    # Pivot the data to have one row per (city_id, year) pair.
    # Using aggfunc='first' ensures that if there are multiple records for 
    # the same (city_id, year, indicator_id) combination, only one is taken.
    # The index will be a MultiIndex of (city_id, year).
    pivoted = df.pivot_table(
        index=['city_id', 'year'],
        columns='indicator_id',
        values='value',
        aggfunc='first'
    )

    # Reset the index to move city_id and year from the index into columns
    pivoted = pivoted.reset_index()

    # To include city_name, we map it back from city_id.
    # We use the first city_name encountered for each city_id in the original dataset.
    city_name_map = df.groupby('city_id')['city_name'].first()
    pivoted['city_name'] = pivoted['city_id'].map(city_name_map)

    # Define the final column order: city_id, city_name, year, then all indicator_ids.
    # Reindexing ensures that all indicator_ids are present as columns,
    # even if they were absent in some city-year combinations (filled with NaN).
    final_cols = ['city_id', 'city_name', 'year'] + indicator_ids
    pivoted = pivoted.reindex(columns=final_cols)

    # Write the pivoted matrix to a CSV file.
    # na_rep='' ensures that NaN values are represented as empty cells.
    # index=False ensures the pandas index is not written as a column.
    pivoted.to_csv('outputs/t11_city_indicator_matrix.csv', index=False, na_rep='')

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

def main():
    # Read the raw Eurostat data
    df = pd.read_csv('outputs/t02_eurostat_raw.csv')

    # Identify all unique indicator_ids in their order of first appearance
    # This ensures we have a complete list of columns to include in the final matrix
    indicator_ids = df['indicator_id'].unique().tolist()

    # Pivot the data to have one row per (city_id, year) pair.
    # Using aggfunc='first' ensures that if there are multiple records for 
    # the same (city_id, year, indicator_id) combination, only one is taken.
    # The index will be a MultiIndex of (city_id, year).
    pivoted = df.pivot_table(
        index=['city_id', 'year'],
        columns='indicator_id',
        values='value',
        aggfunc='first'
    )

    # Reset the index to move city_id and year from the index into columns
    pivoted = pivoted.reset_index()

    # To include city_name, we map it back from city_id.
    # We use the first city_name encountered for each city_id in the original dataset.
    city_name_map = df.groupby('city_id')['city_name'].first()
    pivoted['city_name'] = pivoted['city_id'].map(city_name_map)

    # Define the final column order: city_id, city_name, year, then all indicator_ids.
    # Reindexing ensures that all indicator_ids are present as columns,
    # even if they were absent in some city-year combinations (filled with NaN).
    final_cols = ['city_id', 'city_name', 'year'] + indicator_ids
    pivoted = pivoted.reindex(columns=final_cols)

    # Write the pivoted matrix to a CSV file.
    # na_rep='' ensures that NaN values are represented as empty cells.
    # index=False ensures the pandas index is not written as a column.
    pivoted.to_csv('outputs/t11_city_indicator_matrix.csv', index=False, na_rep='')

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
